messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: DB/ConnSpike service - pgbouncer max_client_conn reached in us-east-1. Auto-page to oncall.

Ash: Acked pager (responded on PD). I'm on it. Any immediate customer reports? :eyes:

Kate: Getting a handful of Zendesk tickets — some timeouts hitting product-search and timeline features. Estimated 4-6 customers seeing elevated 502/504s in us-east.

Lee: Seeing pgbouncer stats: `client_connections` hammered, `server_active` ~120/100 pool size, pgbouncer returning "NO available server" errors. Redis accept-queue also spiked but seems secondary. Suspect cache warmers + batch job ramped up.

Maya: Deploys? Nothing scheduled in last 30m from our side. No config changes.

Sam: Infrastructure metrics: PG replicas healthy but incoming connection attempts per-second jumped x4 at 12:04 UTC. Connection churn is high.

Ash: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily block non-critical background jobs that open lots of DB connections. 2) Increase pgbouncer pool (if safe) or enable fallback to pooled DB host. 3) Rate-limit write-heavy endpoints at the API layer. Who can flip the job toggle?

Kate: I can pause the nightly indexer job (it started early due to backlog). Pausing now.

Lee: Good. Pausing batch jobs should free ~30-40 connections. I can bump pgbouncer `max_client_conn` and `default_pool_size` on the pool for the product cluster — small + roll across 3 pods. Doing a quick config change with low-risk splay.

Lee: Pushing change to pgbouncer config now:

```bash
kubectl apply -f pgbouncer-configmap.yaml --namespace prod-db
# changed default_pool_size: 20 -> 30
# changed max_client_conn: 1000 -> 1500
```

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ash. Escalation path: oncall -> db-lead -> eng-platform if no progress in 10m.

Maya: While Lee rolls, I'm going to temporarily enable API rate limiting for the top noisy routes (search, bulk-sync) and put a 5rps cap per IP/service token. Pushing rule to WAF now.

Ash: Good. Kate — any customer comms needed? Are SLAs impacted?

Kate: For now small set of customers. I'll draft a short status line: "We are investigating intermittent request errors in us-east for a subset of customers; engineers are mitigating. We'll update in 15 minutes." Posting in incidents channel and CS queue.

Lee: pgbouncer patch rolled to 1/3 pods. Metrics show client_conn dropping from 980 -> 720 on the patched pod. No errors in logs so far. Rolling remaining pods.

Sam: Redis accept-queue still showing high `aof_rewrite` latency on one node, but connection backlog is lowering as pgbouncer rolls. Might be a cache stampede. Recommend enabling simple cold-cache throttling for warmers.

Ash: Action list updated: pause indexers (Kate) — done. pgbouncer roll (Lee) — in progress. WAF rule (Maya) — in progress. Monitor + customer comms (Kate) — in progress. Sam to investigate Redis node.

Lee: Roll completed across all pgbouncer pods ~12:18 UTC. System-level "NO available server" errors dropped to near zero. Active connections stabilized ~450.

Sam: Redis node I/O had a short spike; I flushed a stuck client and evicted a non-essential cache namespace for 20m to reduce memory pressure. Accept-queue fell back to normal.

Maya: WAF caps deployed. We're seeing a ~35% reduction in request volume to noisy endpoints. 5xx rate down from 6% -> 0.8% in us-east.

Kate: Updated CS: initial message posted. Will prepare a follow-up in 30m if things remain stable.

Ash: Great work. Can we capture root-cause hypothesis: small number of aggressive background jobs + cache warmers caused connection churn -> pgbouncer exhausted server pools -> app requests started failing. Remediation: better job backpressure, pgbouncer pool autoscale, and circuit-breaker at API layer.

Lee: Agreed. I'll open a post-incident ticket with proposed mitigations: 1) enforce connection pooling for batch jobs, 2) PG connection pool autoscaling playbook, 3) add a pgbouncer health probe that returns degraded before "NO available server" errors.

Maya: I'll add WAF-based temporary throttles to the runbook and a checkbox to enable them automatically on similar alert signatures.

Kate: CS follow-up drafted and scheduled. No major customers escalated so far.

Ash: Handoff: I'm leaving at 12:40 UTC. Next oncall Lee will own the follow-ups and the PD incident until resolved. Lee, please ack handoff.

Lee: Acked. I'll track the postmortem and ensure follow-ups get prioritized.

incident-bot: Incident closed by Ash (manual close) at 12:46 UTC. Summary: mitigations applied, service returned to normal, follow-ups created.

Ash: Marking stable. If anything reappears ping me in #eng-oncall or call. Thanks team :tada:
